transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, yeah—thanks. So, I guess the main thing is at work. I process insurance claims, and I keep getting up from my desk during the day even when I know I’m supposed to stay there and finish reviewing them. It’s kind of embarrassing because it’s not like I don’t know what I’m supposed to be doing.

Like, I’ll stand up to get water or just… walk over somewhere, and then I’m thinking about something totally unrelated, like whether I paid my phone bill or what I’m making for dinner, and then I realize I’ve been away from my workstation again. But yeah, the big reason I came in is that I can’t seem to stay put long enough to get through my claim reviews the way I’m expected to.
Do you find yourself getting distracted by your surroundings or thoughts while you're working?

Yeah, definitely. Like, if people near me start talking about another claim, even if it’s not mine, my brain just kind of… turns toward that instead of what I’m reading. Or I’ll suddenly remember some random errand, like needing to pick up laundry detergent or something, and then I’m gone from the claim in front of me.

Then I look back and realize I didn’t take in any of that section, so I have to reread the same paragraph a few times. It’s frustrating because it’s not hard material exactly, it’s just like my attention slides off it.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're sitting still?

Yeah, I think so. Like in trainings or those longer team meetings, I’m usually doing something—bouncing my leg, clicking my pen, shifting around in the chair. I try to look like I’m paying attention, but then I notice my foot’s been going the whole time.

It’s funny, the chairs in our conference room are really uncomfortable too, so I used to blame that, but it’s not just that. I just kind of can’t sit completely still for very long.
Do you experience these difficulties with focus and restlessness outside of your job as well?

Um… outside of work, I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I notice I get kind of scattered sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s the same thing or just normal life stuff.

Like, at home I’ll start doing one thing and then end up thinking about, I don’t know, whether I need to buy groceries, and then somehow I’m looking at my kitchen cabinets because one of the hinges is loose—actually I’ve been meaning to fix that for weeks. But I guess I haven’t really tracked it the way I have at work, because work is where people notice and there are actual deadlines and stuff.

So… maybe? I’m not sure. What do you mean exactly by outside of my job?
Did you have trouble paying attention or sitting still when you were a kid?

Yeah… I think so, looking back. It’s funny because I wouldn’t have said that before, like I didn’t think of myself as a “problem kid” or anything. I was more the kid teachers said was smart, but then on report cards they’d write stuff like I lost worksheets, or I didn’t follow the instructions, or I needed reminders to finish classwork.

My mom actually kept some of those old comments in a folder somewhere—she keeps everything, like even old appliance manuals from microwaves we don’t own anymore, which is… anyway. But yeah, it wasn’t brand new as an adult. In elementary school there were definitely notes about me missing what the teacher said or not finishing unless someone came by and reminded me.
Did you often get into trouble for running, climbing, or playing too rough when you were a kid?

I don’t really know. I mean, I was a kid, so I’m sure I ran around sometimes, but I don’t remember being, like, the kid who was always climbing on furniture or getting yelled at for being too rough.

My brother was more that kind of kid—he broke this lamp once trying to jump from the couch to the chair, and somehow I got blamed at first because I was in the room, which still annoys me a little. But for me specifically… I don’t think that was a big thing? I’d have to ask my mom if there were stories I’m forgetting.
Did you have more trouble following rules or completing tasks compared to your peers when you were in school?

Yeah, I think so… at least with completing tasks. Not so much like I was constantly breaking rules on purpose or anything, but teachers would write that I was bright and then, you know, I’d lose worksheets or miss part of the instructions and need someone to remind me to finish classwork.

It’s weird, because at the time I just thought everyone got those comments sometimes. And my mom kept some of those report cards in this big folder—she keeps everything, like warranty cards from appliances we haven’t had in years—but looking back, yeah, it seems like it was showing up even in elementary school.
Did you experience difficulties with focus, restlessness, or completing tasks consistently throughout your childhood and adolescence?

Yeah, I mean… looking back, it does seem like it was pretty consistent, at least with the focus and finishing stuff. It wasn’t like it suddenly started now.

In elementary school my teachers would say I was bright, which I remember because my mom really liked that part, but then the same comments would say I lost worksheets, or missed instructions, or needed reminders to finish classwork. She kept some of those old report cards in this folder—she keeps everything, honestly—but yeah, those kinds of notes were there early on.
Have you ever interrupted others or blurted out answers before they finished speaking?

Um… I’m not totally sure. I don’t think I was known for that, exactly? Like, I’m sure I’ve accidentally talked over people before—everyone does sometimes—but I don’t have a clear memory of teachers constantly saying I blurted out answers or anything.

I did sometimes answer too fast if I thought I knew what someone was asking, but then again, my uncle does that all the time at family dinners and everyone just kind of talks over each other, so it’s hard to tell what’s “interrupting” versus just… how people talk. But yeah, I wouldn’t say that was a big complaint I heard about me.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others or finishing their sentences for them?

I don’t know if I’d say often. I mean, I probably do it sometimes, especially if I think I know where someone’s going, but I’m not sure it’s a pattern people complain about.

Finishing sentences… maybe occasionally with people I’m close to? Like my sister and I do that, but she also does it back, so I don’t know if that counts or if it’s just conversation. At work I try pretty hard not to, because in claims calls and stuff you kind of have to let people finish explaining, even if they’re taking the long way around. Which, honestly, I also take the long way around sometimes—like right now.

So… not something I’ve really noticed as a big issue, I guess.
Do you often act on impulse without fully thinking through the consequences?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think of myself as super impulsive, like doing wild things without thinking. But then, I guess it depends what you mean by “act on impulse.”

Like, if you mean buying something randomly because I saw it online… I mean, I’ve done that, but also who hasn’t? My cousin sends me these deals all the time and then suddenly I’m looking at headphones I don’t even need. But I wouldn’t say I’m constantly making huge decisions without thinking them through.

So… maybe sometimes with small stuff, but I don’t know if it’s often or really a major problem.
Did you have more trouble with organization and time management compared to your peers when you were in school?

Yeah… I mean, in school I remember organization being kind of hard, but it’s clearer to me now at work, honestly. Like since my caseload got bigger, my claim folders and notes and email flags just kind of end up all over the place. I’ll have one thing half-marked in the system, then a sticky note, then an email I flagged but forgot why I flagged it.

And then I spend too much time trying to figure out which policy review I’m supposed to tackle first instead of just doing it. It reminds me of school a little, like when I’d have different notebooks or folders and somehow still not know what was due first. But yeah—compared to other people, I guess it did seem like I had to work harder to keep things in order.
Do you feel like your difficulties with focus, restlessness, or completing tasks are causing problems in your relationships or daily life outside of work?

Yeah… outside of work is harder to say, because I kind of measure everything by work lately. Like even when I’m home, I’m thinking about the files I didn’t finish, or whether I missed some detail in a policy note.

The big issue right now is my supervisor actually put me on performance coaching because my claim files are falling behind and they’re questioning my accuracy. Which feels… embarrassing, honestly. I was trying to get onto the senior adjuster track, and now I’m worried I’m messing that up or could lose the chance completely.

So daily life-wise, yeah, it’s spilling over because I’m stressed about it even when I’m not there. But the concrete problem is mostly work.
Do you often feel a strong need to be active and doing something, like you can't just relax and be still?

Yeah, kind of. I don’t know if I’d say I need to be active like I’m going out running around or anything, but sitting still can be weirdly hard.

Like in trainings or longer team meetings, I’ll catch myself bouncing my leg the whole time, clicking my pen, shifting around in the chair. Sometimes I’m trying to look like I’m paying attention, especially if my supervisor’s there, but then I realize I’ve been tapping for like ten minutes. It’s not even that I’m trying to be annoying, it just kind of happens.
Have your difficulties with focus, restlessness, or completing tasks caused problems in your personal relationships?

I’m not totally sure, honestly. I mean, I wouldn’t say people are like… sitting me down and saying I’m ruining the relationship or anything.

Sometimes I wonder if I’m not as present as I should be, but then I start thinking about, like, whether that’s just normal stress or me overthinking it. Like my brother will text me about some random family plan, and then I’ll be thinking about an email I forgot to send, and then suddenly it’s two days later—but I don’t know if that’s what you mean by “caused problems.”

So… I guess I haven’t noticed a clear relationship problem the way I have at work. It’s more fuzzy, if that makes sense.
Did you experience difficulties with focus or restlessness in multiple settings, such as at home, with friends, or in other activities outside of work and school?

I’m not totally sure how to separate that out, honestly. Like, at home I do notice I’ll start doing one thing and then somehow end up opening my phone or thinking about something else, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing or just… normal.

With friends, I guess I’m usually okay? I mean, sometimes I’ll drift a little if we’re just sitting around talking, but then again everybody checks out sometimes. It’s harder for me to point to a clear example outside of work or school and say, “Yes, this is definitely the same problem.”

So I guess my answer is… maybe, but I’m not really sure. Work is where it’s obvious to me.
Did you experience difficulties with focus or restlessness before the age of 12?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, looking back, it wasn’t like this suddenly started when I got older.

In elementary school, I remember teachers writing stuff like I was bright, but I’d lose worksheets or miss instructions. My mom kept some of those old report cards in this folder somewhere—actually she keeps everything, like receipts from 2008 for no reason—but yeah, the comments were kind of the same theme. Like I needed reminders to finish classwork, or I’d be sitting there not done because I hadn’t followed what we were supposed to do.

At the time I don’t think anyone made a huge deal out of it, because I wasn’t trying to cause trouble or anything. But yeah, before 12, I think it was there.
Have you noticed these difficulties with focus and restlessness continuing at the same level into your adult life outside of work?

I’m not sure I can really say it’s the same level outside of work. Like, work gives me a really obvious structure to compare against—deadlines, emails, claims, all that stuff—so it’s easier to notice when I’m slipping.

At home it’s more… vague. I’ll have moments where I’m like, “Was I just spacing out?” but then I’ll get distracted thinking about whether that counts, or whether everyone does that after a long day. And outside of work, like with errands or just hanging out, I don’t know that I’ve tracked it closely enough.

So I guess I don’t have a clear answer. It probably shows up sometimes, but I can’t honestly say I’ve noticed it continuing at the same level outside of work.
Do you often do things on impulse without thinking them through?

I don’t think so? I mean, not in a big way that stands out to me.

I might do small stuff without thinking, like buy a snack I didn’t need or click on something and then realize I’ve been looking at random reviews for, like, kitchen knives when I don’t even cook that much. Actually my roommate has this one knife that’s weirdly nice, and he’s very intense about it, like he sharpens it with this whole stone thing—

Sorry, what was the question exactly? Impulse, right. Yeah, I guess I don’t really see myself as someone who does major impulsive things without thinking them through. At least nothing comes to mind right away.
Do you often find yourself doing things without thinking them through?

I mean… I don’t really know. Not often in a way that I’d be like, “Wow, that was reckless,” you know?

I do little automatic things, like open my phone and suddenly I’m on some random page, or I’ll start doing something and then realize I didn’t really decide to do it. But if you mean big decisions or like, doing risky stuff without considering it, I don’t think that’s really me.

Sorry, I feel like I’m answering the same thing weirdly. I guess my answer is: not that I’ve really noticed.

In elementary school, I remember teachers writing stuff like I was bright, but I’d lose worksheets or miss instructions. My mom kept some of those old report cards in this folder somewhere—actually she keeps everything, like receipts from 2008 for no reason—but yeah, the comments were kind of the same theme. Like I needed reminders to finish classwork, or I’d be sitting there not done because I hadn’t followed what we were supposed to do.

At the time I don’t think anyone made a huge deal out of it, because I wasn’t trying to cause trouble or anything. But yeah, before 12, I think it was there.

doctor.intent: Determine if symptoms have persisted consistently into adulthood
doctor.question: Have you noticed these difficulties with focus and restlessness continuing at the same level into your adult life outside of work?

target_item.reason: The question asks about whether symptoms continued into adult life outside of work, but the provided profile items do not specifically cover adult-life persistence outside work or non-work settings.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I can really say it’s the same level outside of work. Like, work gives me a really obvious structure to compare against—deadlines, emails, claims, all that stuff—so it’s easier to notice when I’m slipping.

At home it’s more… vague. I’ll have moments where I’m like, “Was I just spacing out?” but then I’ll get distracted thinking about whether that counts, or whether everyone does that after a long day. And outside of work, like with errands or just hanging out, I don’t know that I’ve tracked it closely enough.

So I guess I don’t have a clear answer. It probably shows up sometimes, but I can’t honestly say I’ve noticed it continuing at the same level outside of work.

I don’t think so? I mean, not in a big way that stands out to me.

I might do small stuff without thinking, like buy a snack I didn’t need or click on something and then realize I’ve been looking at random reviews for, like, kitchen knives when I don’t even cook that much. Actually my roommate has this one knife that’s weirdly nice, and he’s very intense about it, like he sharpens it with this whole stone thing—

Sorry, what was the question exactly? Impulse, right. Yeah, I guess I don’t really see myself as someone who does major impulsive things without thinking them through. At least nothing comes to mind right away.

patient.answer:
I mean… I don’t really know. Not often in a way that I’d be like, “Wow, that was reckless,” you know?

I do little automatic things, like open my phone and suddenly I’m on some random page, or I’ll start doing something and then realize I didn’t really decide to do it. But if you mean big decisions or like, doing risky stuff without considering it, I don’t think that’s really me.

Sorry, I feel like I’m answering the same thing weirdly. I guess my answer is: not that I’ve really noticed.
